2026-12-06.title: Second Sunday of Advent
readings: Comfort, O comfort my people; prepare the way of the Lord
Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation
We wait for new heavens and a new earth
Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight
2026-12-06.verse: He proclaimed, “The one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the thong of his sandals. I have baptized you with water; but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
theo: Isaiah 40 opens the “Book of Consolation”. After decades of exile God speaks tenderly: “Comfort, O comfort my people… Speak tenderly to Jerusalem.” The punishment is over; a road is to be built in the desert for God to lead his people home; valleys raised, mountains lowered. And the God who comes is a Shepherd who “will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom”.

Mark begins his Gospel with no birth story. Its first words are a title: “The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” Then he quotes Isaiah and Malachi, and John the Baptist appears in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins. People come from all Judea and Jerusalem, confessing their sins. John points away from himself: “The one who is more powerful than I is coming… he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

Peter's letter explains the delay of the Lord's return: “with the Lord one day is like a thousand years… The Lord is not slow about his promise… but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.” God's patience is time given for conversion. So: “Since you are waiting for these, strive to be found by him at peace, without spot or blemish.” Advent is the time to straighten the crooked road of our hearts.
conn: The Book of Consolation.
Scholars call Isaiah 40–55 the Book of Consolation, addressed to the exiles in Babylon (6th century BC). Its first word in Hebrew, nahamu, “comfort”, is doubled for emphasis.
A road for a king.
Ancient kings had roads levelled before their visits. Isaiah pictures a royal highway built for God himself to lead the exiles home.
Mark's first line.
“The beginning of the good news” echoes Genesis 1:1, “In the beginning”. The Gospel is a new creation.
John's clothing.
Mark 1:6 says John wore camel's hair and a leather belt, exactly like Elijah (2 Kings 1:8). The reader is meant to see Elijah returning before the Lord's day (Malachi 4:5).
Untying sandals.
Untying a master's sandals was a slave's task; rabbinic tradition said a disciple should do everything for his teacher except that. John says he is unworthy even of the slave's task.
A thousand years as one day.
2 Peter 3:8 quotes Psalm 90:4. God's time is not ours; his delay is mercy.
altar: At the beginning of Mass we say: “I confess to almighty God…” As at the Jordan, the people of God come confessing their sins and preparing the way.
John baptised with water; Christ baptises with the Holy Spirit. In the Eucharist the Spirit is called down (the epiclesis) upon the gifts and upon us, so that we may become one body.
outline: Ask: what road needs repairing in your heart before Christmas?
God's first word to sinners is tenderness.
Repentance levels the mountains of pride and fills the valleys of discouragement.
Point 3 · He will baptize with the Holy Spirit
John points to Christ; so must we.
The Shepherd carrying a lamb close to his heart.
live: Make a good Advent Confession (Mark 1:5)
Like the crowds at the Jordan, confess your sins this week.
Comfort someone (Isaiah 40:1)
Speak tenderly to someone who is discouraged.
Use God's patience (2 Peter 3:9)
Choose one conversion you have postponed and begin it now.
Point to Christ (Mark 1:7)
Do one good deed this week without seeking credit.
fathers: Origen
“Prepare the way of the Lord within your hearts… The way we prepare for the Lord is a way within, in the heart.”
St Gregory the Great
He explains that the valleys filled are the humble raised, and the mountains brought low are the proud humbled.
St Augustine
“John was the voice that lasts for a time; Christ is the Word who was in the beginning.”
magis: John the Baptist, the Lord's immediate precursor.
saints: 7 Dec: St Ambrose. 8 Dec: Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. 9 Dec: St Juan Diego. 12 Dec: Our Lady of Guadalupe.
2026-12-06.prayer: Almighty and merciful God, may no earthly undertaking hinder those who set out in haste to meet your Son, but may our learning of heavenly wisdom gain us admittance to his company. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2026-12-13.title: Third Sunday of Advent (Gaudete Sunday)
readings: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me; I will greatly rejoice in the Lord
My soul rejoices in my God
Among you stands one whom you do not know
2026-12-13.alt: Gaudete Sunday. Rose vestments may be worn; the rose candle of the Advent wreath is lit. The memorial of St Lucy is not celebrated this year because it falls on Sunday.
2026-12-13.verse: John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
theo: The Entrance Antiphon gives this Sunday its name: “Gaudete in Domino semper”, “Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice. The Lord is near” (Philippians 4:4–5). Halfway through Advent the violet softens to rose. Joy is not a break from Advent; it is its heart, because the One we await is already near.

Isaiah's servant says, “The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.” Jesus will read these very words in the synagogue at Nazareth and say, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled” (Luke 4:21). The response today is Mary's Magnificat: Christian joy is the joy of the humble whom God has lifted up.

John the Evangelist presents the Baptist as a witness: “He himself was not the light, but he came to testify to the light.” When priests and Levites ask who he is, John answers with three “No”s: not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet. He is only “the voice”. Then he says something every Advent needs to hear: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Christ is already in our midst, in the Word, the sacraments, the poor, the person beside us; the question is whether we recognise him.

Paul gives the programme for joyful waiting: “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances… Do not quench the Spirit… Hold fast to what is good.” And he ends with a promise: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.” Holiness is God's work in us; our joy rests on his faithfulness.
conn: Why rose?
Rose (not pink) vestments are worn only twice a year: Gaudete Sunday in Advent and Laetare Sunday in Lent. The colour signals that the penitential season is half over and the feast is near.
Gaudete.
The Latin word means “Rejoice!” (plural imperative), the first word of the Entrance Antiphon from Philippians 4:4.
Three “No”s and one “Yes”.
John denies being the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet (Deuteronomy 18:15). His one positive claim is to be a voice (Isaiah 40:3). A voice exists for the sake of the word it carries.
Isaiah 61 and Nazareth.
Jesus' inaugural sermon in Luke 4:16–21 reads Isaiah 61:1–2, stopping before “the day of vengeance of our God”. He proclaims the year of favour.
The Magnificat as psalm.
Today the response is not a psalm but Mary's song (Luke 1:46–55), sung daily at Vespers throughout the Church.
“Among you stands one whom you do not know.”
St Augustine saw in this verse Christ's hidden presence: he is near even when unrecognised.
altar: At every Mass the deacon or priest says, “The Lord be with you.” It is John's message turned into a greeting: Christ stands among us.
Before Communion we hear, “Behold the Lamb of God”, the words John the Baptist spoke when he saw Jesus (John 1:29). The voice points; the Word is given.
outline: Light the rose candle. Ask: what is your reason to rejoice this week?
Point 1 · Anointed to bring good news
Isaiah 61, fulfilled in Jesus at Nazareth.
Joy of the humble, like Mary's Magnificat.
Point 3 · One whom you do not know
Christ is already among us; recognise him.
The rose candle in the middle of violet: joy in the middle of waiting.
live: Rejoice in the Lord (1 Thessalonians 5:16)
Each night this week, name three things that made you rejoice.
Pray without ceasing (5:17)
Pray a short prayer each time you wash your hands or pick up your phone.
Recognise him (John 1:26)
Look for Christ in one person you usually overlook.
Bring good news to the poor (Isaiah 61:1)
Visit a lonely or sick person before Christmas.
fathers: St Augustine
“John was the voice; Christ is the Word. The voice passes; the Word remains.”
St Bernard of Clairvaux
He writes that the joy of Advent is the joy of a heart that knows the Lord is coming to it.
St Gregory the Great
He notes John's humility: questioned about his greatness, he answered by pointing to another.
magis: The joy of the Gospel fills the hearts of those who encounter Jesus.
John, the voice of the Spirit.
saints: 14 Dec: St John of the Cross. 17 Dec: the O Antiphons begin; the final days of Advent.
2026-12-13.prayer: O God, who see how your people faithfully await the feast of the Lord's Nativity, enable us, we pray, to attain the joys of so great a salvation and to celebrate them always with solemn worship and glad rejoicing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2026-12-20.title: Fourth Sunday of Advent
readings: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever
For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord
The mystery kept secret for long ages is now disclosed
You will conceive in your womb and bear a son
2026-12-20.alt: Year B. Liturgical colour: violet. O Antiphon of the day: O Key of David.
2026-12-20.verse: Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
theo: On the last Sunday of Advent the readings bring two houses face to face. King David, settled in his cedar palace, wants to build a house for the ark of God. Through Nathan, God turns the offer around: “Are you the one to build me a house to live in?… the LORD will make you a house.” God promises David a dynasty, an heir whose throne “shall be established forever”. David wanted to give God a house; God gives David a house, a family line, a future.

In Nazareth the angel Gabriel tells Mary that the promise to David is now fulfilled: her son “will be called the Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give to him the throne of his ancestor David. He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.” The everlasting house God promised is not made of cedar but of flesh: the Son of God will dwell in the womb of a virgin. Mary herself becomes the house of God, the Ark of the New Covenant.

Mary's question, “How can this be, since I am a virgin?”, is not doubt but a request for understanding. The answer is the Holy Spirit and the power of the Most High overshadowing her, the same verb used of the cloud over the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35). The Church professes that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary (CCC 484–486). And Mary gives her free consent: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.” Paul calls this “the mystery that was kept secret for long ages but is now disclosed”, made known to all nations to bring about “the obedience of faith”.
conn: Two houses.
In Hebrew bayit means both a building and a dynasty. God refuses David's building but promises him a dynasty (2 Samuel 7:11, 16). The wordplay runs through the whole chapter.
Overshadow.
Luke 1:35 uses episkiazō, the word used in the Greek Old Testament for the cloud of God's glory resting on the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35). Mary becomes the new dwelling of God.
The Ark of the New Covenant.
The Fathers saw in Mary the true Ark: the old ark carried the tablets of the Law, manna and Aaron's rod; Mary carries the Word, the Bread of Life and the true Priest.
O Key of David.
Today's O Antiphon: “O Key of David and sceptre of the house of Israel, who open and no one shuts: come and lead the prisoners from the prison house” (cf. Isaiah 22:22).
“The obedience of faith”.
Paul's phrase (Romans 16:26; 1:5) is exactly what Mary lives at the Annunciation: obedience that comes from faith (CCC 144, 148).
Nazareth.
An unimportant village not mentioned in the Old Testament. God's greatest promise is fulfilled in an obscure place, to a young woman nobody had heard of.
altar: At every Mass, in the Creed, we bow at the words “and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man”. On Christmas and the Annunciation we kneel.
As Mary received the Word in her womb, we receive the Word made flesh in Communion. Her “let it be with me” is the model of every “Amen” we say before receiving the Body of Christ.
outline: Ask: have you ever wanted to do something great for God, and found that God wanted to do something greater for you?
David wants to build God a house; God builds David a house.
Point 2 · The promise fulfilled in Mary
The Son of the Most High on David's throne forever.
Mary's free yes, the obedience of faith.
The cedar palace and the humble house of Nazareth.
“Let it be with me according to your word.”
live: Make room (2 Samuel 7)
Before Christmas, clear one space in your day, your home or your heart for God.
Say Mary's yes (Luke 1:38)
Pray the Angelus three times a day this week.
Be overshadowed (Luke 1:35)
Spend quiet time before the Blessed Sacrament before Christmas.
Prepare the crib
Set up the crib with your family, placing the Child only on Christmas night.
fathers: St Bernard of Clairvaux
In his famous homily he imagines the whole world waiting for Mary's answer: “Answer quickly, O Virgin. Speak the word, and receive the Word.”
St Irenaeus
“The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary.”
St Augustine
He says Mary conceived Christ first in her heart by faith before conceiving him in her womb.
magis: Conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary.
Mary's fiat: the obedience of faith.
Mary, not merely passive, cooperated freely in salvation.
saints: 21 Dec: St Peter Canisius. 23 Dec: St John of Kanty. 25 Dec: Christmas. 26 Dec: St Stephen.
2026-12-20.prayer: Pour forth, we beseech you, O Lord, your grace into our hearts, that we, to whom the Incarnation of Christ your Son was made known by the message of an Angel, may by his Passion and Cross be brought to the glory of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2026-12-25.title: The Nativity of the Lord (Christmas) · Solemnity
readings: All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God
All the ends of the earth have seen the saving power of God
God has spoken to us by a Son
The Word became flesh and lived among us
2026-12-25.alt: Mass during the Day. Mass during the Night: Isaiah 9:1–6; Psalm 96; Titus 2:11–14; Luke 2:1–14. Mass at Dawn: Isaiah 62:11–12; Psalm 97; Titus 3:4–7; Luke 2:15–20. Holy day of obligation. Liturgical colour: white.
2026-12-25.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: Christmas has three Masses, and together they tell the whole mystery. At night, Luke's Gospel: the census, Bethlehem, the manger, the angels' “Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favors.” At dawn, the shepherds who go with haste and find the child, and Mary who “treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart”. In the day, John's Prologue lifts our eyes from the manger to eternity: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God… And the Word became flesh and lived among us.”

The child in the manger is not a man who became God, nor God pretending to be human. He is the eternal Son, true God from true God, who “for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man”. The Church teaches that he is one Person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion or division (Council of Chalcedon, 451; CCC 464–469). He “emptied himself” (Philippians 2:7) without ceasing to be God.

Why did he come? Hebrews says: God, who once spoke “in many and various ways by the prophets”, has now spoken “to us by a Son”. Christmas is God's final word, and the word is a child. He came to save us from sin, to make us “partakers of the divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4; CCC 460), to show us the Father, and to give us a model of holiness. “To all who received him… he gave power to become children of God.” St Leo the Great's Christmas sermon gives the response: “Christian, remember your dignity.”

Isaiah sings of the messenger's beautiful feet on the mountains announcing peace, and of watchmen shouting for joy. Tonight the shepherds are those watchmen, and we are invited to join them. The manger points to the altar: born in Bethlehem, “House of Bread”, laid in a feeding trough, the Child will give himself as the Bread of Life.
conn: Three Masses.
Since the 6th century Rome has celebrated three Christmas Masses: at night (at St Mary Major's crib chapel), at dawn and in the day. Each priest may celebrate all three.
Bethlehem, House of Bread.
Beit Lechem means “house of bread”. The Bread of Life is born in the House of Bread and laid in a manger, a place where animals eat.
Bands of cloth.
The “swaddling clothes” foreshadow the linen cloths of the tomb (Luke 23:53); the Fathers saw birth and burial joined.
The census.
Luke dates the birth by a census under Caesar Augustus (Luke 2:1). The emperor thought he ruled the world; the true King was born in his territory, counted among his subjects.
John's Prologue.
The first words, “In the beginning”, echo Genesis 1:1. Christmas is a new creation. For centuries John 1:1–14 was read at the end of every Mass as the “Last Gospel”.
The crib.
St Francis of Assisi set up the first living crib at Greccio in 1223 so that people could see with their eyes the poverty of the Child (Pope Francis, Admirabile Signum, 2019).
altar: At Christmas we kneel in the Creed at the words “and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man”. The whole Church bows before the mystery.
The Word who became flesh in Bethlehem becomes present on the altar under the forms of bread and wine. Every Mass is a little Christmas: the Lord comes again among us, humble and hidden.
outline: Ask: if God wanted to speak one final word to humanity, what would it be? It is a child.
True God and true man: the mystery of the Incarnation.
Point 2 · God speaks by a Son
Christmas is God's last and fullest word.
To all who received him he gave power to become children of God.
The manger in the House of Bread, and the altar.
live: Make room (Luke 2:7)
There was no room in the inn. Invite someone lonely to your Christmas meal.
Kneel at the crib
Pray before the crib as a family: thank Jesus for coming.
Ponder like Mary (Luke 2:19)
Spend ten silent minutes with the Christmas Gospel.
Bring peace
Reconcile with someone during the Christmas octave.
fathers: St Leo the Great
“Christian, remember your dignity, and now that you share in God's own nature, do not return by sin to your former base condition.”
St Augustine
“He who made man was made man… the Bread was hungry, the Fountain thirsted, the Light slept, the Way was tired from the journey.”
St Athanasius
“He became what we are so that he might make us what he is.”
magis: On the meaning of the Christmas crib.
saints: 26 Dec: St Stephen. 27 Dec: Holy Family (St John). 28 Dec: Holy Innocents. 1 Jan: Mary, Mother of God.
2026-12-25.prayer: O God, who wonderfully created the dignity of human nature and still more wonderfully restored it, grant, we pray, that we may share in the divinity of Christ, who humbled himself to share in our humanity. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2026-12-27.title: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph · Feast
readings: Your heir shall be your own son
The Lord remembers his covenant for ever
The faith of Abraham, Sarah and Isaac
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom
2026-12-27.alt: Year B. These readings may be replaced by those common to all years: Sirach 3:2–6, 12–14; Psalm 128; Colossians 3:12–21. Liturgical colour: white. Sunday within the Octave of Christmas.
2026-12-27.verse: The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him.
theo: On the Sunday after Christmas the Church looks at the home in which the Son of God chose to grow up. He did not come as an adult from nowhere; he came as a child into a family, with a mother, a foster father, a village, relatives and the Law of Moses. The Second Vatican Council calls the family “the domestic church” (Lumen Gentium 11), and the Holy Family of Nazareth is its model.

This year's readings put faith at the centre of family life. Abraham, childless and old, is told to look at the stars: “So shall your descendants be.” And “he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.” Sarah conceives Isaac at the time God had promised. Hebrews praises their faith: Abraham set out “not knowing where he was going”, and later offered Isaac, trusting that God could raise the dead. A family is built not first on money or plans but on trust in God's promise.

In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple to present him to the Lord, as the Law prescribed for the firstborn (Exodus 13:2), offering the gift of the poor, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”. Simeon takes the child in his arms and blesses God; he also tells Mary that her son will be “a sign that will be opposed” and that “a sword will pierce your own soul too”. Even the Holy Family was not spared sorrow. Then they return to Nazareth, where “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom”. The hidden years at Nazareth sanctify ordinary family life: work, prayer, obedience and love (CCC 531–533).
conn: The domestic church.
The phrase goes back to St John Chrysostom and was taken up by Vatican II (Lumen Gentium 11; CCC 1655–1658). Parents are the first teachers of the faith.
The offering of the poor.
Leviticus 12:8 allowed a poor family to offer two birds instead of a lamb. Mary and Joseph offered the gift of the poor, while presenting the true Lamb of God.
Presentation and purification.

The Law required the redemption of the firstborn son (Exodus 13:2, 12–13) and the purification of the mother forty days after birth (Leviticus 12). The Church celebrates this scene again on 2 February.
Abraham and Isaac.
Hebrews 11:19 says that Abraham received Isaac back “figuratively speaking” from the dead. The Fathers saw in Isaac carrying the wood a figure of Christ carrying his Cross.
Two elderly witnesses.
Simeon and Anna stand for faithful Israel waiting for God's promise. The young family and the old saints meet in the Temple.
Nazareth.
Jesus spent about thirty years in Nazareth and only about three in public ministry. Most of the life of the Saviour was ordinary family life.
altar: The family gathers around the altar each Sunday as the family of God. Children learn the faith first by seeing their parents pray and receive the Eucharist.
At the Presentation, Jesus is offered to the Father in the Temple. At every Mass he offers himself to the Father, and we offer our families with him.
outline: Ask: what is the one thing that holds your family together?
Abraham and Sarah trusted God's promise.
Mary and Joseph give Jesus back to God, and hear of the sword.
The child grows in wisdom in an ordinary home.
The small house at Nazareth with a carpenter's bench.
“The favor of God was upon him.”
live: Pray together (Luke 2:22)
Begin or renew family prayer: even ten minutes each evening.
Bless your children
Make the Sign of the Cross on your children's foreheads before sleep.
Honour the elderly (Luke 2:25–38)
Visit or call grandparents and older relatives during the Christmas season.
Consecrate your family
Consecrate your family to the Holy Family of Nazareth.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
He urged Christian parents to make their home a church, where the Scriptures are read and prayers are said together.
St Paul VI (Nazareth, 5 January 1964)
He called Nazareth a school of silence, of family life and of work, where we learn what the life of Jesus was like.
magis: The family as the domestic church.
St John Paul II, Familiaris Consortio 86
“The future of humanity passes by way of the family.”
The Holy Family of Nazareth as model for families.
The hidden life at Nazareth; the domestic church.
saints: 28 Dec: Holy Innocents. 29 Dec: St Thomas Becket. 31 Dec: St Sylvester I. 1 Jan: Mary, Mother of God.
2026-12-27.prayer: O God, who were pleased to give us the shining example of the Holy Family, graciously grant that we may imitate them in practising the virtues of family life and in the bonds of charity, and so, in the joy of your house, delight one day in eternal rewards. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

2026-12-01.title: Tuesday of the First Week of Advent
readings: The Spirit of the Lord shall rest on him
Justice shall flourish in his time, and fullness of peace for ever
Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit
2026-12-01.verse: Blessed are the eyes that see what you see! For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but did not see it.
theo: Isaiah sees a shoot coming out of the stump of Jesse, the cut-down family tree of David. On this shoot the Spirit of the Lord rests: wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge and fear of the Lord. These are the gifts the Church sees fulfilled in Christ and shared with us in Confirmation (CCC 1831). Under his rule the wolf lives with the lamb and “the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD”.

In the Gospel Jesus, “rejoicing in the Holy Spirit”, thanks the Father for revealing these things not to the wise and intelligent but to “infants”. Then he tells his disciples that they see what prophets and kings longed to see. Advent invites us to become little enough to receive, and to recognise how blessed we are to know Christ.
outline: Ask: what new life can God bring from a cut-down stump in your life?
Point 1 · A shoot from the stump
God begins again from what seems dead.
Point 2 · The Spirit rests on him
The seven gifts of the Messiah, shared with us.
Blessed are the eyes that see.
“Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.”
live: Pray for the gifts (Isaiah 11:2)
Each day this week pray for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
Become little (Luke 10:21)
Ask a child a question about God and listen to the answer.
2026-12-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, shoot from the stump of Jesse, let your Spirit rest on me too. Make me little enough to receive what you reveal, and grateful to see what prophets and kings longed to see. Amen.

2026-12-02.title: Wednesday of the First Week of Advent
readings: The Lord will make a feast for all peoples
I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life
Jesus heals many and feeds the multitude
2026-12-02.verse: I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way.
theo: Isaiah promises a mountain banquet for all peoples, rich food and fine wine, and more: God “will swallow up death forever” and “wipe away the tears from all faces”. In the Gospel that promise begins to come true on a mountain by the Sea of Galilee. Crowds bring the lame, the blind, the mute; Jesus heals them. Then, moved with compassion, he takes seven loaves and a few fish, gives thanks, breaks them and gives them to the disciples to distribute. All eat and are filled, with seven baskets left over.

The words “took, gave thanks, broke, gave” are the words of the Last Supper. Advent prepares us to receive the One who is Bread from heaven, born in Bethlehem, whose name means “house of bread”. And the disciples are his hands: Christ multiplies what we bring, but asks us to distribute it to the hungry.
outline: Ask: who in your neighbourhood will go hungry this week?
Point 1 · A feast for all peoples
God promises joy, plenty and the end of death.
Jesus sees the crowd and is moved.
Point 3 · Took, gave thanks, broke, gave
The Eucharist and our mission to the hungry.
live: Feed someone (Matthew 15:32)
Give a meal or groceries to a needy family this week.
Give thanks before meals
Say grace before every meal this Advent.
2026-12-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, compassionate Shepherd, you healed the sick and fed the hungry on the mountain. Feed me with your Bread of life, and make my hands generous to those who have nothing to eat. Amen.

2026-12-03.title: Thursday of the First Week of Advent · St Francis Xavier, Priest
readings: Trust in the Lord forever, for the Lord is an everlasting rock
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord
2026-12-03.alt: Memorial of St Francis Xavier, priest, patron of the missions. In the Archdiocese of Goa and Daman it is a solemnity, with proper readings.
2026-12-03.verse: Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
theo: Jesus ends the Sermon on the Mount with a warning and a picture. Not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” will enter the Kingdom, but the one who does the Father's will. Two houses face the same rain, floods and wind; one stands because it is founded on rock. Isaiah gives the foundation's name: “Trust in the LORD forever, for in the LORD GOD you have an everlasting rock.” Advent is a time to check the foundations.

St Francis Xavier (1506–1552), Jesuit, one of the first companions of St Ignatius, arrived in Goa in 1542 and preached along the coasts of South India, among the Paravas of the Fishery Coast, in Travancore, then in Malacca, the Moluccas and Japan. He died on the island of Shangchuan, within sight of China. His body rests in the Basilica of Bom Jesus in Goa. He built on rock: “Lord, I am here; what do you want me to do?”
outline: Ask: if a storm hit your life tonight, what would hold you up?
Build on God, the everlasting Rock.
A life poured out for the Gospel in India and Asia.
live: Check your foundation (Matthew 7:24)
Choose one teaching of Jesus you hear but do not do, and act on it this week.
Pray for missionaries (St Francis Xavier)
Pray for missionaries from Kerala serving in North India and abroad.
2026-12-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, everlasting Rock, let me not only call you “Lord” but do your will. Build my life on your word, and through the prayers of St Francis Xavier, make me a missionary wherever I am. Amen.

2026-12-04.title: Friday of the First Week of Advent
readings: On that day the eyes of the blind shall see
The Lord is my light and my salvation
Two blind men believe in Jesus and are healed
2026-12-04.alt: First Friday of the month. Optional memorial: St John Damascene, priest and doctor.
2026-12-04.verse: Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you.”
theo: Isaiah describes the transformation God will bring: Lebanon becomes a fruitful field, “the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see”, the meek find joy, the tyrant disappears. Advent is the season of this hope.

Two blind men follow Jesus crying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!” They call him by his messianic title, though they cannot see him. In the house Jesus asks them one question: “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” “Yes, Lord.” He touches their eyes: “According to your faith let it be done to you.” Their eyes are opened. Faith sees before the eyes do. St John Damascene, remembered today, defended the veneration of icons: in Christ the invisible God has become visible, and we may look on his face.
outline: Ask: what are you unable to see in your life right now?
Jesus asks for faith before he heals.
Point 3 · The Lord is my light
“According to your faith let it be done to you.”
live: Answer his question (Matthew 9:28)
Tell Jesus in prayer: “Yes, Lord, I believe you can do this,” naming your need.
First Friday
Go to Confession or spend time before the Blessed Sacrament.
2026-12-04.prayer: Son of David, have mercy on me. Touch the eyes of my heart, increase my faith, and be my light and my salvation this Advent. Amen.

2026-12-05.title: Saturday of the First Week of Advent
readings: He will be gracious to you when you cry
Blessed are all who wait for the Lord
He had compassion for them; the harvest is plentiful
2026-12-05.alt: Optional: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2026-12-05.verse: When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
theo: Isaiah speaks tenderly to a people in distress: God “waits to be gracious to you”; “he will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry”; your Teacher will no longer hide, and “your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, ‘This is the way; walk in it.’” He promises rain, harvest, and the day when the Lord “binds up the injuries of his people”.

Jesus goes through all the towns teaching, proclaiming and healing. Seeing the crowds “harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd”, he is moved with compassion. His response is twofold: pray (“ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers”) and send (he calls the Twelve and gives them authority). “You received without payment; give without payment.” Advent compassion becomes mission.
outline: Ask: when did someone show you the way when you were lost?
Point 1 · God waits to be gracious
He hears our cry and shows the way.
Pray for labourers, and become one.
“This is the way; walk in it.”
live: Pray for vocations (Matthew 9:38)
Pray daily this Advent for priests, religious and lay missionaries.
Give freely (Matthew 10:8)
Offer a free service to someone this week: tuition, a ride, a visit.
2026-12-05.prayer: Lord of the harvest, you wait to be gracious to us. Show me the way and let me walk in it. Send labourers into your harvest, and make me generous, giving freely what I have freely received. Amen.

2026-12-07.title: Monday of the Second Week of Advent · St Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor
readings: Here is your God; he will come and save you
Our God will come to save us!
Friend, your sins are forgiven you
2026-12-07.alt: Memorial of St Ambrose, bishop and doctor of the Church.
2026-12-07.verse: When he saw their faith, he said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven you.”
theo: Isaiah 35 is a song of the desert in bloom: “The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad… Strengthen the weak hands… Say to those who are of a fearful heart, ‘Be strong, do not fear! Here is your God… He will come and save you.’” Then the eyes of the blind are opened, the lame leap like a deer, and the redeemed walk the Holy Way home with singing.

In the Gospel the prophecy walks into a crowded house. Friends cannot get their paralysed companion near Jesus, so they open the roof and lower him down. “When he saw their faith”, Jesus first forgives his sins, then, to show that “the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”, tells him to stand up and walk. The deepest healing is forgiveness; the first miracle Advent asks for is a good Confession. St Ambrose, bishop of Milan, preached this mercy and baptised St Augustine at Easter 387.
outline: Ask: whom are you carrying to Jesus in prayer?
Friends carry the paralysed man to Jesus.
“Here is your God; he will come and save you.”
live: Carry someone (Luke 5:19)
Bring a friend's need to Jesus in prayer every day this week.
Receive forgiveness (Luke 5:24)
Go to Confession this Advent.
2026-12-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of the friends and forgave the paralysed man. Strengthen my weak hands, make the dry places of my life bloom, and give me the joy of your forgiveness. Amen.

2026-12-08.title: The Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Solemnity
readings: I will put enmity between your offspring and hers
Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous deeds
He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless
Greetings, favoured one! The Lord is with you
2026-12-08.alt: Solemnity. Patronal feast of many dioceses and churches. Liturgical colour: white.
2026-12-08.verse: And he came to her and said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
theo: Today the Church celebrates that Mary, from the first moment of her conception, was preserved free from all stain of original sin, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the human race. So Pope Pius IX defined it in 1854 (Ineffabilis Deus; CCC 491). This is not about the conception of Jesus (that is the Annunciation) but about Mary's own conception in the womb of her mother, St Anne.

The first reading takes us back to the garden. After the fall God asks, “Where are you?”, and then speaks the first promise of redemption: “I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head.” The Fathers called this the Protoevangelium, the first Gospel. The New Eve, whose Son crushes the serpent, was never under the serpent's power.

The angel greets Mary as kecharitōmenē, “full of grace” or “highly favoured”: one who has been and remains filled with God's grace. Mary's sinlessness is not her own achievement; she too was redeemed by Christ, but “in a more exalted fashion” (CCC 492), preserved rather than rescued. Paul says God “chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love”. What God did fully in Mary from the first moment, he wants to do in us through Baptism and a lifetime of grace.

And Mary's freedom shines in her answer: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” Grace does not crush freedom; it frees it. Where Eve said no, Mary says yes. The Immaculate Conception in the middle of Advent shows us how God prepares a dwelling for his Son, and how we may prepare too.
conn: Pius IX defined the dogma on 8 December 1854. Four years later at Lourdes, the Lady told Bernadette, a poor girl who did not understand the words: “I am the Immaculate Conception.”
Kecharitōmenē.
Luke 1:28 uses a perfect passive participle of the verb for “to grace”: Mary has been graced and remains so. It is used as her name, as if “Full-of-Grace” were what God calls her.
The Protoevangelium.
Genesis 3:15 is called the “first Gospel” because it is the first announcement of the Redeemer and of his mother's share in his victory (CCC 410–411).
The debate.

Great saints like Bernard and Thomas Aquinas hesitated, because all need Christ's redemption. Bl. John Duns Scotus (d. 1308) gave the key: Mary was redeemed by preservation, the most perfect redemption.
Patroness.
The Immaculate Conception is patroness of the United States, Brazil, the Philippines and many dioceses; many churches in Kerala bear this title.
Eve and Mary.
St Irenaeus (2nd century): “The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by Mary's obedience.”
altar: The Preface of today's Mass sings that God preserved Mary from all stain of original sin, “so that in her, endowed with the rich fullness of your grace, you might prepare a worthy Mother for your Son.”
As Mary was prepared to receive the Word in her womb, we prepare to receive him at the altar. Before Communion we say with the centurion: “Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word.”
outline: Ask: if God could prepare a perfect home for his Son, what would it look like? It looks like Mary.
Point 1 · Where are you? The first promise
After the fall, God promises the woman and her offspring.
Mary preserved from sin by Christ's grace, from her first moment.
Grace frees Mary's yes; Eve's knot is loosed.
The woman clothed with the sun, crushing the serpent.
“Here am I, the servant of the Lord.”
live: Pray the Hail Mary slowly
Meditate on each phrase of the Hail Mary today.
Answer “Where are you?” (Genesis 3:9)
Make an honest examination of conscience and go to Confession.
Say yes (Luke 1:38)
Say yes to one thing God is asking of you this Advent.
Honour Mary at home
Place flowers before Mary's image and pray the Rosary as a family.
fathers: St Irenaeus
“The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary; what the virgin Eve bound by unbelief, the Virgin Mary set free by faith.”
St Ephrem the Syrian
“You alone and your Mother are wholly beautiful in every way; for there is no stain in you, Lord, nor any blemish in your Mother.”
St Andrew of Crete
He calls Mary's conception “the beginning of feasts”, the first step of salvation.
magis: Mary, adorned from her first instant with a holiness entirely unique.
saints: 9 Dec: St Juan Diego. 12 Dec: Our Lady of Guadalupe. 13 Dec: St Lucy.
2026-12-08.prayer: O God, who by the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son, grant, we pray, that, as you preserved her from every stain by virtue of the Death of your Son, which you foresaw, so, through her intercession, we, too, may be cleansed and admitted to your presence. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2026-12-09.title: Wednesday of the Second Week of Advent
readings: The Lord gives strength to the weary
O bless the Lord, my soul!
Come to me, all you that are weary
2026-12-09.alt: Optional memorial: St Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin.
2026-12-09.verse: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
theo: Isaiah speaks to exiles who think God has forgotten them: “My way is hidden from the LORD.” The prophet answers: the Creator of the stars, who calls each by name, “does not faint or grow weary… He gives power to the faint… those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” Waiting on God is not passive; it is where strength comes from.

Jesus speaks the same promise in person: “Come to me, all you that are weary… I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.” A yoke joins two animals to share a load; Jesus offers to carry our burden with us. St Juan Diego, a humble Mexican Indian, was the one Our Lady sent to the bishop in 1531; God chose the weary and little to carry his message.
outline: Ask: what burden are you carrying alone right now?
The Creator gives strength to the faint.
“My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
live: Bring your burden (Matthew 11:28)
Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament and hand over one burden.
Share someone's yoke
Help someone who is overloaded this week.
2026-12-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, I come to you tired and burdened. Take my yoke with me, renew my strength, and teach me to wait on you and rise on eagles' wings. Amen.

2026-12-10.title: Thursday of the Second Week of Advent
readings: I, the Lord your God, hold your right hand
The Lord is gracious and merciful; slow to anger, and of great kindness
No one greater than John the Baptist has arisen
2026-12-10.alt: Optional memorial: Our Lady of Loreto.
2026-12-10.verse: Truly I tell you, among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
theo: “For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; it is I who say to you, ‘Do not fear, I will help you.’” Isaiah calls Israel a “worm”, small and weak, yet God will make it a threshing sledge. For the poor and thirsty he opens rivers on bare heights and turns the desert into pools, “so that all may see and know… that the hand of the LORD has done this.”

Jesus praises John the Baptist: no one born of women is greater. Yet “the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he”. John stands at the threshold; the disciples of Jesus enter the Kingdom through Baptism and become children of God. Greatness in the Kingdom is not our achievement but God's gift, received by the little ones who let God take their hand.
outline: Ask: when did you last feel God holding your hand?
Point 1 · I hold your right hand
God's personal care for the weak.
Point 3 · The least in the Kingdom
Baptism gives us a greatness beyond John's.
“Do not fear, I will help you.”
live: Hold out your hand (Isaiah 41:13)
When afraid today, open your right hand in prayer and say: “Lord, hold me.”
Thank God for Baptism (Matthew 11:11)
Find out your baptism date and celebrate it.
2026-12-10.prayer: Lord my God, you hold my right hand and say, “Do not fear.” Open rivers in the dry places of my life, and make me little enough to enter your Kingdom. Amen.

2026-12-11.title: Friday of the Second Week of Advent
readings: O that you had paid attention to my commandments!
Those who follow you, Lord, will have the light of life
We played the flute for you, and you did not dance
2026-12-11.alt: Optional memorial: St Damasus I, pope.
2026-12-11.verse: Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.
theo: God speaks with a father's longing: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go. O that you had paid attention to my commandments! Then your prosperity would have been like a river.” God's commandments are not burdens imposed from outside; they are the way to peace that flows like a river.

Jesus compares his generation to sulky children in the marketplace who will play neither wedding nor funeral. John came fasting, and they said he had a demon; the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they called him “a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners”. Some hearts will find an excuse against any messenger. But “wisdom is vindicated by her deeds”: the fruit of God's work shows its truth. Advent asks us to stop making excuses and to respond.
outline: Ask: what excuse do you use to avoid what God is asking?
Point 1 · God teaches for our good
Let our lives show God's wisdom.
“O that you had paid attention to my commandments!”
live: Drop an excuse (Matthew 11:17)
Name one excuse you keep using with God and drop it today.
Meditate on the Law (Psalm 1:2)
Read one of the Ten Commandments each day with the Catechism's explanation.
2026-12-11.prayer: Lord my God, you teach me for my good and lead me in the way I should go. Free me from the excuses that keep me from responding, and let my life show the wisdom of your ways. Amen.

2026-12-12.title: Saturday of the Second Week of Advent · Our Lady of Guadalupe
readings: Elijah, a prophet like fire, will return
Lord, make us turn to you; let us see your face and we shall be saved
Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him
2026-12-12.alt: Optional memorial of Our Lady of Guadalupe (a feast in the Americas, with proper readings: Zechariah 2:14–17 or Revelation 11:19a; 12:1–6a, 10ab; Luke 1:26–38 or 1:39–47).
2026-12-12.verse: I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but they did to him whatever they pleased.
theo: Sirach praises Elijah: “a prophet like fire, and his word burned like a torch”. Taken up in a whirlwind, he is destined to return “to turn the hearts of parents to their children, and to restore the tribes of Jacob” (cf. Malachi 4:5–6). Coming down from the mountain of the Transfiguration, the disciples ask about this. Jesus answers that Elijah has already come, in John the Baptist, “and they did not recognize him”; the Son of Man too will suffer.

Today the Church in the Americas honours Our Lady of Guadalupe, who appeared in 1531 to St Juan Diego near Mexico City, as a young mestiza woman speaking his language, leaving her image on his cloak (tilma). Within a few years millions of indigenous people were baptised. Like Elijah, like John, Mary prepares the way for Christ and turns hearts. Her image shows her pregnant: Advent in a picture, carrying Christ to a whole people.
outline: Ask: whom has God sent to prepare your heart, and did you recognise them?
Point 2 · They did not recognise him
John came, and many missed him.
She carries Christ to a people.
live: Turn hearts at home (Sirach 48:10)
Reconcile with a family member before Christmas.
Recognise God's messengers (Matthew 17:12)
Thank someone whose words helped your faith.
2026-12-12.prayer: Lord God, you sent Elijah and John to prepare your way, and Mary to bring your Son to every people. Turn my heart to you and to my family, and let me recognise your messengers. Amen.

2026-12-14.title: Monday of the Third Week of Advent · St John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor
readings: A star shall come out of Jacob
Teach me your ways, O Lord
By what authority are you doing these things?
2026-12-14.alt: Memorial of St John of the Cross, priest and doctor of the Church.
2026-12-14.verse: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near—a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel.
theo: Balaam was a pagan seer hired to curse Israel, but the Spirit of God came upon him and he could only bless. He sees from afar: “a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel.” The Fathers saw this fulfilled in the star the Magi followed to Bethlehem. God can speak truth even through unexpected mouths.

In the Temple the chief priests challenge Jesus: “By what authority are you doing these things?” He answers with a question about John's baptism: from heaven or human? They calculate and refuse to answer. Truth requires honesty; the leaders preferred safety. St John of the Cross, the Carmelite mystic, wrote that we must pass through the “dark night” of purification to reach union with God, and: “In the evening of life, we will be examined in love.”
outline: Ask: how do you respond when God's truth is inconvenient?
Christ's authority comes from the Father.
live: Answer honestly (Matthew 21:27)
Face one truth about yourself you have been avoiding.
Pray in the dark (St John of the Cross)
Spend ten minutes in silent prayer, even if you feel nothing.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord, star rising from Jacob, teach me your ways. Give me an honest heart that does not calculate but obeys, and lead me, like St John of the Cross, through every dark night to union with you. Amen.

2026-12-15.title: Tuesday of the Third Week of Advent
readings: I will leave in the midst of you a people humble and lowly
The Lord hears the cry of the poor
The tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him
2026-12-15.verse: For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.
theo: Zephaniah condemns a proud city that “has listened to no voice” and promises a different future: God will purify the lips of the peoples, and “I will leave in the midst of you a people humble and lowly. They shall seek refuge in the name of the LORD.” This humble remnant is the true Israel of Advent: Mary, Joseph, Zechariah, Elizabeth, the shepherds.

Jesus tells of two sons. One refuses to work in the vineyard but later changes his mind and goes; the other says yes but does not go. The religious leaders gave God many words; tax collectors and prostitutes gave him their repentance. “Even after you saw it, you did not change your minds.” Advent asks not for fine words but for a changed heart. It is never too late to turn and go into the vineyard.
outline: Ask: are you a “yes, Lord” person who never goes?
Point 1 · A humble and lowly people
God builds his future with the humble.
The son who changed his mind did the Father's will.
Repentance opens the door of the Kingdom.
“They shall seek refuge in the name of the Lord.”
live: Turn a no into a yes (Matthew 21:29)
Do something you refused God earlier.
Choose humility (Zephaniah 3:12)
Let someone else have the credit today.
2026-12-15.prayer: Lord, the poor cry out and you hear them. Make me humble and lowly, change my heart where I have said no to you, and let my yes be more than words. Amen.

2026-12-16.title: Wednesday of the Third Week of Advent
readings: Let the clouds rain down the Just One, and the earth bring forth a Saviour
Go and tell John what you have seen and heard
2026-12-16.verse: And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.”
theo: “Shower, O heavens, from above, and let the skies rain down righteousness; let the earth open, that salvation may spring up.” This verse became the famous Advent chant Rorate caeli. Heaven and earth cooperate: grace comes down, and the earth (the Virgin's womb) brings forth the Saviour. God says, “There is no other god besides me… Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth!”

From prison John sends disciples to ask Jesus: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?” Jesus does not answer with a title but with evidence: the blind see, the lame walk, the poor hear good news, Isaiah's signs fulfilled. “Blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.” Even the greatest prophet had to trust a Messiah different from what he expected.
outline: Ask: what do you do when Jesus doesn't act the way you expect?
Point 1 · Rain down the Just One
Heaven and earth meet in the Incarnation.
“Blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.”
live: Bring your doubts (Luke 7:20)
Tell Jesus honestly any doubt you carry, as John did.
Be a sign (Luke 7:22)
Do one work of mercy that shows Christ to someone.
2026-12-16.prayer: Rain down, O heavens, the Just One; let the earth bring forth a Saviour. Lord Jesus, when I doubt, show me your works, and keep me from taking offence at your ways. Amen.

2026-12-17.title: 17 December · Advent Weekday (O Wisdom)
readings: The scepter shall not depart from Judah
Justice shall flourish in his time, and fullness of peace for ever
The genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham
2026-12-17.alt: From today the readings follow the date. The “O Antiphons” begin at Vespers and as Gospel Acclamations: today, O Sapientia (O Wisdom).
2026-12-17.verse: An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
theo: Today the final stretch of Advent begins. The readings now follow the calendar date, and the Church sings the great “O Antiphons”. Today's: “O Wisdom, who came from the mouth of the Most High, reaching from end to end and ordering all things mightily and sweetly: come and teach us the way of prudence” (cf. Wisdom 8:1). Jacob blesses Judah: “The scepter shall not depart from Judah… until tribute comes to him; and the obedience of the peoples is his.”

Matthew opens with a genealogy: forty-two generations in three groups of fourteen, from Abraham to David to the exile to Christ. It contains saints and sinners, kings and nobodies, and, unusually, four women (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah), some foreigners, some with complicated stories. God's plan runs through real, messy family history. Then the pattern breaks: “Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born.” Jesus enters our family tree as a true man and true Son of God.
outline: Ask: do you know your family tree? Who in it would you rather not mention?
Christ, the Wisdom of God, orders all things.
God keeps his promises across centuries.
“Of whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah.”
live: Pray for your family tree (Matthew 1:1)
Pray today for your ancestors, living and dead, by name.
Pray the O Antiphon
Pray today's O Antiphon each morning and evening.
2026-12-17.prayer: O Wisdom, who came forth from the mouth of the Most High, reaching from end to end and ordering all things mightily and sweetly: come and teach us the way of prudence. Bless my family and all its history. Amen.

2026-12-18.title: 18 December · Advent Weekday (O Adonai)
readings: I will raise up for David a righteous Branch
Justice shall flourish in his time, and fullness of peace for ever
Jesus is born of Mary, betrothed to Joseph, son of David
2026-12-18.alt: O Antiphon: O Adonai (O Lord and Ruler of the house of Israel).
2026-12-18.verse: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O Adonai, and leader of the house of Israel, who appeared to Moses in the fire of the burning bush and gave him the law on Sinai: come and redeem us with outstretched arm.” Jeremiah promises: “I will raise up for David a righteous Branch… And this is the name by which he will be called: ‘The LORD is our righteousness.’”

Matthew tells the story from Joseph's side. Mary is found with child; Joseph, “a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace”, plans to dismiss her quietly. In a dream the angel tells him the child is from the Holy Spirit and gives him two tasks: take Mary as your wife, and name the child Jesus, “for he will save his people from their sins”. By naming him, Joseph makes Jesus legally a son of David. All this fulfils Isaiah: “the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel, God is with us.” Joseph awakes and obeys, without a word recorded.
outline: Ask: when did God ask you to change your plans?
God raises a just King from David's line.
A just man who listened and obeyed.
He saves from sin; God is with us.
“He will save his people from their sins.”
live: Obey promptly (Matthew 1:24)
Do at once one thing God has been asking of you.
Honour St Joseph
Pray to St Joseph for fathers and for families in difficulty.
2026-12-18.prayer: O Adonai, Lord who spoke to Moses in the burning bush, come and redeem us with outstretched arm. Give me the faith of St Joseph to listen, to trust and to obey, and let Jesus be born in my home. Amen.

2026-12-19.title: 19 December · Advent Weekday (O Root of Jesse)
readings: The birth of Samson is announced
My mouth shall be filled with your praise, and I will sing your glory!
The birth of John the Baptist is announced
2026-12-19.alt: O Antiphon: O Radix Jesse (O Root of Jesse).
2026-12-19.verse: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.”
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O Root of Jesse, who stand as a sign for the peoples, before whom kings shall keep silence and whom the nations shall seek: come and deliver us, and delay no longer” (cf. Isaiah 11:10). Two barren couples receive good news. An angel tells Manoah's wife she will bear a son, Samson, a nazirite consecrated to God from the womb. In the Temple, the angel Gabriel tells the old priest Zechariah that Elizabeth will bear a son, John, “filled with the Holy Spirit” even before his birth, who will go before the Lord “with the spirit and power of Elijah”.

Zechariah doubts and becomes mute until the promise is fulfilled. His silence is not only punishment; it is a time of waiting, of interior listening, that will burst into the Benedictus at John's birth. Elizabeth rejoices: “This is what the Lord has done for me… he looked favourably on me and took away the disgrace I have endured.” In the last days of Advent, God turns barrenness into life, silence into song.
outline: Ask: what in your life feels barren?
God gives life where none seemed possible.
Samson and John belong to God from the start.
live: Keep a holy silence (Luke 1:20)
Spend fifteen minutes in silence today, without phone or noise.
Pray for childless couples
Pray for couples longing for children, and for all who wait.

2026-12-21.title: 21 December · Advent Weekday (O Dayspring)
readings: Look, my beloved comes, leaping upon the mountains
Exult, you just, in the Lord! Sing to him a new song
2026-12-21.alt: O Antiphon: O Oriens (O Dayspring). Optional memorial: St Peter Canisius, priest and doctor.
2026-12-21.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O Dayspring, splendour of eternal light and sun of justice: come and enlighten those who dwell in darkness and the shadow of death.” On the shortest days of the year in the northern hemisphere, the Church sings of the Sun that rises from on high. The Song of Songs gives the voice of the bride: “The voice of my beloved! Look, he comes, leaping upon the mountains.”

Mary, having said yes, does not stay at home. She “set out and went with haste” to the hill country to visit Elizabeth. At her greeting, John leaps in his mother's womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, cries out: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb… And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” The first person to call Jesus “Lord” in Luke's Gospel is an unborn child's mother, and the first to rejoice at his presence is an unborn child. Elizabeth's last word praises Mary's faith: “Blessed is she who believed.”

2026-12-22.title: 22 December · Advent Weekday (O King of Nations)
readings: Hannah gives thanks for the birth of Samuel
My heart exults in the Lord, my Saviour
The Mighty One has done great things for me
2026-12-22.alt: O Antiphon: O Rex Gentium (O King of Nations).
2026-12-22.verse: He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty.
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O King of the nations and their desire, the cornerstone who makes both one: come and save the human race, which you fashioned from clay.” Hannah, once barren and mocked, brings the child Samuel to the house of the Lord at Shiloh and gives him back to God: “For this child I prayed… Therefore I have lent him to the LORD.” Her song (today's responsorial psalm) sings of a God who “raises up the poor from the dust”.

Mary's Magnificat echoes Hannah's song almost line by line. The humble servant of Nazareth magnifies the Lord who “has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant”. Then she sings of a great reversal: the proud scattered, the powerful brought down, the lowly lifted up, the hungry filled, the rich sent away empty. This is not a political programme but the logic of the Kingdom: God's power is shown in mercy to the humble. The Church sings the Magnificat every evening at Vespers.

What God gives, Hannah gives back.

“The Mighty One has done great things for me.”

2026-12-23.title: 23 December · Advent Weekday (O Emmanuel)
readings: I will send you the prophet Elijah before the day of the Lord comes
Lift up your heads and see; your redemption is near at hand
The birth of John the Baptist
2026-12-23.alt: O Antiphon: O Emmanuel. Optional memorial: St John of Kanty, priest.
2026-12-23.verse: He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And all of them were amazed. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.
theo: The last O Antiphon: “O Emmanuel, our King and Lawgiver, the hope of the nations and their Saviour: come and save us, O Lord our God.” Malachi, the last of the prophets, announces a messenger who will prepare the way, and the Lord who will suddenly come to his temple, like a refiner's fire. He will send Elijah “to turn the hearts of parents to their children”.

In the Gospel the messenger is born. Neighbours rejoice with Elizabeth because the Lord has shown great mercy to her. At the circumcision they want to call the child Zechariah, after his father, but Elizabeth says, “No; he is to be called John.” Zechariah, mute for nine months, writes, “His name is John”, and his tongue is freed to praise God. John means “The Lord has shown favour”. The name is not the family's choice but God's gift: this child belongs to God's plan. “What then will this child become?” For “the hand of the Lord was with him.”
outline: Ask: what does your name mean, and who chose it?
God's favour breaks the silence into praise.
“The hand of the Lord was with him.”

2026-12-23.prayer: O Emmanuel, our King and Lawgiver, hope and Saviour of the nations, come and save us, O Lord our God. As you freed Zechariah's tongue, open my lips to praise you, and let your hand be with me. Amen.

2026-12-24.title: 24 December · Advent Weekday (Morning Mass)
readings: The kingdom of David shall endure forever before the Lord
For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord

2026-12-24.alt: Morning Mass of 24 December. In the evening the Vigil Mass of Christmas is celebrated (Isaiah 62:1–5; Acts 13:16–17, 22–25; Matthew 1:1–25).
2026-12-24.verse: By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
theo: On the last morning of Advent the Church sings with Zechariah. Filled with the Holy Spirit, the old priest who had been silent for nine months bursts into the Benedictus, the song the Church prays every morning at Lauds. He blesses God who “has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them” and has “raised up a mighty savior for us in the house of his servant David”, the promise of 2 Samuel 7 now fulfilled.

Then he turns to his own child: “And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways.” And the song ends with the image of dawn: “the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness.” Tonight that dawn breaks. Advent ends not with a lecture but with a song of praise and a sunrise.

2026-12-26.title: Saint Stephen, the First Martyr · Feast
readings: Into your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit
It is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father
2026-12-26.alt: Feast, within the Octave of Christmas. Liturgical colour: red.
2026-12-26.verse: While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
theo: The day after Christmas the Church wears red. It can seem a sudden change, from the crib to the stones. But the Fathers saw the connection: “Yesterday Christ was born on earth so that today Stephen might be born in heaven” (St Fulgentius). The Child came to give his life; those who follow him may be asked to give theirs. Christmas is not sentimental; it is the beginning of a love that goes to the Cross.

Stephen, “full of grace and power”, was one of the seven deacons chosen to serve the poor (Acts 6:1–6). He also preached with wisdom no one could withstand, as Jesus had promised (Matthew 10:19–20). Accused before the council, he saw “the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God”. As he was stoned he prayed two prayers that echo Jesus' own on the Cross: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit” and “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” The martyr is the perfect disciple: he dies like his Master.

Standing nearby, holding the coats of the stoners, was a young man named Saul (Acts 7:58). St Augustine said: “If Stephen had not prayed, the Church would not have had Paul.” Forgiveness is never wasted; it bears fruit we may never see.
conn: The first martyr.
Stephen is called the Protomartyr, the first to die for Christ after Pentecost. His name means “crown” in Greek.
Two prayers from the Cross.
Compare Luke 23:46 (“Father, into your hands I commend my spirit”) and Luke 23:34 (“Father, forgive them”). Luke wrote both his Gospel and Acts and deliberately shows Stephen dying like Jesus.
The Son of Man standing.
Elsewhere Christ is seated at God's right hand. Here he stands, as if rising to welcome his witness or to plead his cause.
A deacon.

Stephen was among the first seven deacons, ordained to serve at tables so that the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the word (Acts 6:2–6). Service of the poor and witness to the truth belong together.
Saul at the stoning.
Acts 7:58 introduces Saul, the future St Paul, holding the cloaks. Stephen's forgiving prayer is followed, two chapters later, by Saul's conversion.
Wenceslas.
The carol “Good King Wenceslas” is set on the Feast of Stephen, when the king goes out in the snow to bring food to a poor man.
altar: In the Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I), after the consecration, Stephen is the first name in the list of saints: “John the Baptist, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas…”
The Eucharist gives the strength of the martyrs. The same Christ who strengthened Stephen comes to us under the form of bread to make us faithful witnesses.
outline: Ask: why does the Church wear red the day after Christmas?
Point 1 · Full of grace and power
A deacon who served and preached.
Stephen sees Jesus standing to receive him.
Point 3 · Lord, do not hold this sin against them
The crib and the stones: love that goes to the end.

fathers: St Fulgentius of Ruspe
“Yesterday our King, clothed in flesh, came forth from the Virgin's womb; today his soldier, leaving the tent of his body, went triumphant to heaven.”
St Augustine
“If Stephen had not prayed, the Church would not have had Paul.”

He calls Stephen the first to follow in the footsteps of the Lord's Passion.
magis: Martyrdom, the supreme witness to the truth of the faith.
Forgiveness: “as we forgive those who trespass against us”.

2026-12-26.prayer: Grant, Lord, we pray, that we may imitate what we worship, and so learn to love even our enemies, for we celebrate the heavenly birthday of a man who knew how to pray even for his persecutors. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2026-12-28.title: The Holy Innocents, Martyrs · Feast
readings: The blood of Jesus cleanses us from all sin
Our soul has escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler
Herod killed all the children in and around Bethlehem
2026-12-28.alt: Feast, within the Octave of Christmas. Liturgical colour: red.
2026-12-28.verse: A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing and loud lamentation, Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be consoled, because they are no more.
theo: Within the joy of Christmas the Church remembers the small boys of Bethlehem killed by King Herod. Herod, afraid of losing his throne to the newborn “king of the Jews”, sent soldiers to kill all the children of two years and under in and around Bethlehem. Bethlehem was a small village, so the number of children was probably small; but each one was a person loved by God.

The Church has honoured these children as martyrs since early times. They could not yet speak or choose, yet they died in place of Christ and because of him. The Church teaches that those who die for the faith before receiving Baptism are saved by this “baptism of blood” (CCC 1258). An ancient sermon read today in the Office of Readings says of them that they confess Christ not by speaking but by dying.

Matthew sees in the scene the fulfilment of Jeremiah: “Rachel weeping for her children”. Rachel, mother of the tribes, weeps over her lost children; and every mother who has lost a child can find her grief named in Scripture. Yet Jeremiah's next words are of hope: “there is hope for your future” (Jeremiah 31:17). The child Jesus escapes to Egypt, as Israel once went down to Egypt, and later the Lord will call his Son out of Egypt (Hosea 11:1).

The first reading reminds us that “God is light and in him there is no darkness at all”, and that Jesus “is the atoning sacrifice for our sins”. Herod's darkness does not have the last word. Today the Church prays for all innocent children who suffer: unborn children, children killed in war, abused or abandoned children, and their grieving parents (CCC 2270–2274).
conn: Herod the Great.

Herod ruled Judea under Rome until his death around 4 BC. Ancient historians record that he killed members of his own family out of fear for his throne. The massacre of a few village children fits his character.
A new Moses.
Pharaoh ordered Hebrew baby boys to be thrown into the Nile (Exodus 1:22), but Moses was saved. Matthew shows Jesus as the new Moses, saved from a murderous king.
Rachel's tomb.
Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin and was buried on the road to Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19). Matthew imagines her weeping again for the children of Bethlehem.
Out of Egypt.
Hosea 11:1 speaks of Israel as God's son called out of Egypt. Jesus relives the history of his people.
Flowers of the martyrs.
The poet Prudentius (4th century) called the Holy Innocents “flowers of the martyrs”, cut down by the frost as they first opened.
Childermas.
In many places this day was called Childermas, and children were specially blessed. In Kerala it is known as the feast of the Kunjipaithangal.
altar: The colour red recalls the blood of the martyrs. At Mass we offer the one Sacrifice of the Lamb, in whose blood the Innocents were washed.
We bring to the altar all suffering children and grieving parents, uniting them to the Child who escaped to Egypt and later died on the Cross.
outline: Ask: why would the Church remember a massacre during Christmas?
God does not ignore the grief of mothers.
Point 3 · The Innocents are with Christ
Martyrs without words; hope for all innocent children.
A small grave on the road to Bethlehem and a Child safe in his mother's arms.
“Let the little children come to me.”

Visit or write to a family that has lost a child.

fathers: St Quodvultdeus
In a sermon read today in the Office of Readings he says that the children, though they cannot speak, bear witness to Christ, and that by Christ's grace infants become martyrs.
Prudentius
His hymn greets them as “flowers of the martyrs” who play with palms and crowns before the altar of God.
magis: The flight into Egypt and the massacre of the innocents.
The protection of human life from conception.
St John Paul II, Evangelium Vitae 18
The defence of the weakest and most innocent.

2026-12-28.prayer: O God, whom the Holy Innocents confessed and proclaimed on this day, not by speaking but by dying, grant, we pray, that the faith in you which we confess with our lips may also speak through our manner of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2026-12-29.title: 29 December · Fifth Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
A light for revelation to the Gentiles
2026-12-29.alt: Optional memorial: St Thomas Becket, bishop and martyr. Liturgical colour: white.
2026-12-29.verse: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
theo: Old Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Guided by the Spirit he comes into the Temple just as Mary and Joseph bring in the child. He takes Jesus in his arms and sings the Nunc Dimittis, which the Church prays every night at Compline: now I can die in peace, for I have seen your salvation.

Simeon's song is universal: the child is “a light for revelation to the Gentiles” as well as the glory of Israel. But he also speaks of contradiction: the child will be “a sign that will be opposed”, and a sword will pierce Mary's soul. The first reading draws the practical lesson: “whoever says, ‘I abide in him,’ ought to walk just as he walked”; whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light. St Thomas Becket, archbishop of Canterbury, killed in his cathedral on this day in 1170, gave his life defending the freedom of the Church.
outline: Ask: what are you waiting for in life? Simeon waited for one thing.
Simeon comes at the right moment.
Christ divides hearts; the sword pierces Mary.

Pray Simeon's song before sleeping tonight.

2026-12-29.prayer: Lord, now let your servant go in peace; your word has been fulfilled. My eyes have seen the salvation you prepared for all peoples. Let me walk in your light and love my brothers and sisters. Amen.

2026-12-30.title: 30 December · Sixth Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: Whoever does the will of God lives forever
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
Anna spoke about the child to all who were looking for redemption
2026-12-30.verse: At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
theo: After Simeon comes Anna, a prophet, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, a widow of great age. She “never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.” A whole life of faithful prayer prepares her to recognise the child at once. She becomes one of the first evangelists: she praises God and speaks about the child to everyone waiting for redemption.

Luke places a man and a woman, Simeon and Anna, side by side as witnesses; both elderly, both full of the Spirit. The elderly have a mission in the Church: to pray, to remember and to pass on the faith (Pope Francis, catecheses on old age, 2022). The first reading warns that “the world and its desire are passing away, but those who do the will of God live forever.” Then the Holy Family returns to Nazareth, and “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom”.
outline: Ask: who taught you to pray? Many of us would name a grandmother.
Anna's long life of prayer and fasting.
Point 2 · She spoke about the child
The first woman to proclaim him in the Temple.
“The favor of God was upon him.”

2026-12-30.prayer: Lord, give me Anna's faithfulness in prayer and her joy in speaking of your Son. Keep me from loving what is passing away, and let me do your will, that I may live forever. Amen.

2026-12-31.title: 31 December · Seventh Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: You have been anointed by the Holy One
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
2026-12-31.alt: Optional memorial: St Sylvester I, pope. Liturgical colour: white. In the evening the Vigil Mass of the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, is celebrated.
2026-12-31.verse: From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.
theo: On the last day of the civil year the Church reads again the Prologue of John: “In the beginning was the Word.” As one year ends and another begins, we remember the One who stands above all time, through whom “all things came into being”, and who entered time to give us “grace upon grace”. The first reading says: “Children, it is the last hour.” Christian time is not an endless circle; it moves towards Christ's return.

It is right to end the year with thanksgiving. The Church traditionally sings the Te Deum on this evening, and grants a plenary indulgence, under the usual conditions, to those who take part in its public recitation on the last day of the year (Enchiridion of Indulgences). We thank God for every grace of the past year, ask pardon for our sins, and entrust the new year to Mary, Mother of God, whose solemnity begins tonight. Pope St Sylvester I, remembered today, led the Church in the years after the persecutions ended.
outline: Ask: what are you most thankful for this year?
Christ is Lord of all time.
Whatever darkness this year held, the light was not overcome.
Count the graces; begin the new year in Christ.
“From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.”

2026-12-31.prayer: We praise you, O God, we acknowledge you to be the Lord. For every grace of this year, thank you; for every sin, forgive us; for the year to come, guide us. From your fullness let us receive grace upon grace. Amen.
