homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the prophet Isaiah begins with a beautiful word: “Comfort, O comfort my people.” After years of exile, God's first word is not anger but tenderness.

And then a voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord.” Every valley lifted up, every mountain made low. In ancient times roads were repaired before a king's visit. Isaiah says: God himself is coming; prepare his road!

Mark begins his Gospel with John the Baptist in the desert. People come from everywhere, confessing their sins and being baptised in the Jordan. That is how the road is prepared: not with decorations but with repentance.

What are the mountains in us? Pride, stubbornness, the refusal to forgive. What are the valleys? Discouragement, laziness, the feeling that I can never change. Advent asks us to bring both to God. Confession is the bulldozer that levels the road!
And John points away from himself: “One more powerful than I is coming… he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.” A true Christian is like John: a finger pointing to Jesus.

St Peter tells us why the Lord seems to delay: “The Lord is not slow about his promise, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish.” This Advent is God's patience with us. Let us not waste it. Make a good Confession. Comfort someone who is low. And prepare the road for the King.
kids: Children, when an important guest is coming, what do we do? We clean the house!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Gaudete Sunday, the Sunday of joy. The priest may wear rose vestments, and we light the rose candle. Why? Because the Lord is near.

The prophet Isaiah says: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me; he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to captives.” Years later Jesus stood in the synagogue of Nazareth, read these words, and said: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled.” Our joy has a name: Jesus.

Instead of a psalm we sing Mary's song: “My soul rejoices in my God.” Mary was poor and humble, and God did great things for her. Christian joy is not the joy of having everything; it is the joy of being loved by God.

In the Gospel people ask John: “Who are you? Are you the Messiah? Elijah? The prophet?” And he says, “No, no, no. I am only a voice.” And then: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Jesus was already there, in the crowd, unnoticed.
Is it the same with us? Jesus is among us: in the Eucharist, in the Word, in the poor at our gate, in the family member we take for granted. Advent asks us to open our eyes.

St Paul gives us a simple programme for this week: “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.” Try it: every night, thank God for three joys. And remember his promise: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.” Rejoice: the Lord is near!
kids: Children, today the candle is pink, I mean rose! It's the candle of joy.
Christmas is getting close, and Jesus is near!
John the Baptist said: Jesus is among you, but you don't know him. Where can we find Jesus? In church, in our family, in poor people.
This week, say thank you to God for three happy things every night!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday before Christmas, the readings tell us about two houses.

King David lived in a palace of cedar. He looked at the ark of God in a tent and felt ashamed: “I live in luxury and God lives in a tent. Let me build God a house.” A good thought. But God answers through the prophet Nathan: “You will build me a house? No, I will build you a house.” God promises David a family line whose throne will last forever.

A thousand years later, in a small village called Nazareth, the angel Gabriel greets a young woman: “You will conceive and bear a son… The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David, and of his kingdom there will be no end.” The promise to David comes true, not in a palace but in a girl's humble home.

Mary asks, “How can this be?” Not doubt, but faith seeking to understand. The angel answers: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.” Just as God's cloud rested on the tent in the desert, God now rests on Mary. She becomes the house of God, the true Ark of the Covenant.

And then her answer: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” With these words, the whole history of salvation turns. St Bernard imagined the whole world holding its breath, waiting for her yes.

Like David, we often want to do great things for God. But God wants first to do great things in us. This Christmas, he asks to make his home in our hearts. Let us make room, like Mary, and say: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
kids: Children, King David wanted to build a big house for God. But God said: I will build a house for you!
Then God chose Mary to be the mother of Jesus. Mary said yes to God.
Jesus wants to live in our hearts too. Can we say yes like Mary?
This week, help set up the crib at home, and leave the manger empty until Christmas night!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and holy Christmas to you all!

Tonight and today the Church tells the story three ways. At night, Luke tells us of the census, the journey to Bethlehem, no room in the inn, the manger, the shepherds and the angels singing, “Glory to God in the highest.” In the day, John lifts our eyes to eternity: “In the beginning was the Word… and the Word became flesh and lived among us.”

Who is this child? Not just a good man, not an angel, but God himself. The eternal Son, through whom everything was made, now lies in a manger, needing his mother's milk. St Augustine marvelled: the Bread was hungry, the Fountain was thirsty, the Light slept. God became small so that we would not be afraid to come close.

Why did he come? The letter to the Hebrews says: long ago God spoke through the prophets, but now he has spoken to us by a Son. Christmas is God's final word to us, and that word is love in the form of a child. He came to forgive our sins, to show us the Father, and to make us God's own children. St John says: “To all who received him, he gave power to become children of God.”

But there was no room in the inn. Is there room in ours? In our busy celebrations, our shopping, our food and decorations, is there room for the Child? And is there room for the poor, the lonely, the migrant, those for whom this Christmas is sad?

Bethlehem means “House of Bread”. The Child was laid in a manger, where animals eat. From the beginning he was preparing to give himself as our food. Today at this altar he comes to us again. Let us receive him with joy, and, as St Leo said, “Christian, remember your dignity.” A blessed Christmas to you and your families!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, two days ago we knelt before the manger. Today the Church asks us to look around the manger: at Mary, at Joseph, at the family into which God chose to be born.

God could have come in any way he wished. He chose to come as a baby, into a family. He needed a mother to feed him, a father to protect him and teach him a trade, and a home where he could grow. That tells us how much God values the family.

Today's first reading shows Abraham and Sarah, old and childless. God tells Abraham to count the stars: so many will be your descendants. And Abraham believed. A family is not built first on property, jobs or plans, but on faith in God.

In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple. They are poor; they can only offer two small birds. Simeon takes the child in his arms and praises God, but also tells Mary that a sword will pierce her heart. Even the Holy Family knew sorrow, fear and uncertainty. If your family is going through hard times, you are not far from Nazareth.

Then the Gospel says simply: they went home to Nazareth, and the child grew, filled with wisdom, and the favour of God was upon him. Thirty quiet years of work, prayer and ordinary love. That is where holiness grows for most of us: at the kitchen table, at work, in patience with each other.
So let us bring our families to the Lord today. Let us pray together at home, forgive each other quickly, respect our elders and bless our children. Jesus, Mary and Joseph, make our homes like yours.
kids: Children, Jesus had a family too: Mary his mother and Joseph his foster father.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today in the middle of Advent we celebrate Mary Immaculate. Some think this feast is about Jesus' conception, but it is about Mary's own conception in her mother's womb. From that first moment God preserved her from original sin.
Why? Because God was preparing a home for his Son. When we expect an important guest, we prepare the house. God prepared the most beautiful home: a soul without any stain of sin.

The first reading takes us to the garden. After the first sin, God calls, “Where are you?” And then he gives the first promise: the woman and her offspring will crush the serpent's head. Mary is that woman. The serpent never had power over her.

But don't think Mary did not need Jesus. She was saved by Jesus too, only in a more wonderful way. We are pulled out of the mud after we fall; Mary was kept from falling. Both are the work of the same Saviour.

And grace did not make Mary a robot. When the angel greeted her, “Full of grace, the Lord is with you,” she asked questions, she thought, and then she freely said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.” Eve said no to God; Mary said yes. St Irenaeus said: Eve tied the knot; Mary untied it.

What God did in Mary from the first moment, he wants to do in us through Baptism, Confession and the Eucharist. Paul says God chose us “to be holy and blameless before him in love”. So today, let us answer God's question, “Where are you?”, honestly. Let us come to Confession, and with Mary say: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
kids: Children, today is Mary's special feast! God made Mary pure and beautiful from the very beginning.
Why? Because she was going to be Jesus' mother, and God wanted a perfect home for his Son.
When the angel came, Mary said: “Yes, God, I will do what you want.”
Today, bring flowers to Mary and say a Hail Mary with your family!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, yesterday we sang carols around the crib. Today the priest wears red, and we hear about stones and death. Why?

An ancient bishop, St Fulgentius, explained: “Yesterday Christ was born on earth so that today Stephen might be born in heaven.” The Child of Bethlehem came to give his life. Christmas is the beginning of a love that will go all the way to the Cross, and those who follow him are invited into that same love.

Stephen was a deacon, chosen to serve the poor widows at table. He was also full of the Holy Spirit and spoke with such wisdom that no one could answer him. When they dragged him out to stone him, he looked up and saw heaven open and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

And listen to his last words: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” And: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” These are almost exactly the words of Jesus on the Cross. Stephen died the way Jesus died, forgiving.

Standing there, holding the coats of those who threw the stones, was a young man named Saul. He later became St Paul, the great apostle. St Augustine said: “If Stephen had not prayed, the Church would not have had Paul.” Forgiveness is never wasted.

So this Christmas, let us ask: is there someone I need to forgive? A family member, a neighbour, a colleague? Let us pray for them by name, as Stephen did. And let us remember the Christians who suffer for their faith today. The joy of Christmas is strong enough to face even this.
kids: Children, today is the feast of St Stephen. He loved Jesus very much.
He helped poor people and told everyone about Jesus. Some people got angry and threw stones at him.
But Stephen did something amazing: he forgave them, just like Jesus did on the Cross.
Is there someone you need to forgive? Say: “Jesus, help me forgive.”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Christmas is a feast of joy, yet today the Church remembers something terrible: the killing of the little children of Bethlehem.

King Herod heard from the wise men that a new king had been born. He was afraid of losing his power. He tried to trick the wise men and, when that failed, he sent soldiers to kill every boy of two years and under in Bethlehem.

But God protected his Son. An angel warned Joseph in a dream: get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt. And Joseph got up that very night and went. Silent, obedient Joseph saved the life of the Saviour.

Matthew recalls the prophet Jeremiah: a voice in Ramah, Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted. Scripture does not hide the grief of mothers. God sees every tear. And the Church honours these children as the first martyrs: they could not speak, but they confessed Christ by dying for him.

Today Herod has many faces. Children are still killed before birth, in wars, through hunger and abuse. The Holy Innocents ask us to stand with the weakest, to protect life from its beginning, and to comfort parents who grieve.
Jesus said: “Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them.” Let us bring all the children of the world to him today, and let us be like Joseph, ready to rise and act to protect them.

By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Begin or renew daily family prayer.

sub: Mary and Joseph offer the gift of the poor.
q: Consecrate to me all the firstborn; whatever is the first to open the womb among the Israelites, of human beings and animals, is mine.

Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.”
points.apply: Offer your children to God in prayer today.

sub: He grew in wisdom and grace.
Faith is passed on at home.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.

Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart. And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Read a Gospel passage together at home this week.

concl: God chose a family; families find God at home.
Jesus, Mary and Joseph, make our homes like yours.
2026-12-27.resolve: Consecrate your family to the Holy Family this week.

intro: Theme: “A shoot from the stump.”
God starts again from what seems dead; his Spirit rests on the Messiah; the little ones see.

sub: David's family tree was cut down.
God begins again where we see an end.
q: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.

At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants; yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.”
points.apply: Bring one “dead stump” in your life to God in prayer.

q: The wolf shall live with the lamb, the leopard shall lie down with the kid, the calf and the lion and the fatling together.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
points.apply: Make peace with one person this Advent.

points.h: Blessed are the eyes that see
sub: Prophets and kings longed to see.
We see Christ in Word and Sacrament.
q: Many peoples shall come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths.”

Then turning to the disciples, Jesus said to them privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see! For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.”
points.apply: Thank God tonight for the gift of faith.

concl: God's new beginnings come from small shoots.
Become little, and you will see.
2026-12-01.resolve: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each morning this Advent.

intro: Theme: “A feast for all peoples.”
God promises a feast; Jesus heals and feeds; the Eucharist sends us to the hungry.

q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.

Then Jesus called his disciples to him and said, “I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way.”
points.apply: Feed someone hungry this week.

sub: Jesus heals the lame, blind and mute.
God's promise is fulfilled in him.
Our sorrows are not the last word.
q: He will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces, and the disgrace of his people he will take away from all the earth, for the LORD has spoken.
He will wipe every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; mourning and crying and pain will be no more, for the first things have passed away.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who is grieving.

sub: The words of the Last Supper.
Christ is the Bread from Bethlehem.
q: The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want.

He took the seven loaves and the fish; and after giving thanks he broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds. And all of them ate and were filled; and they took up the broken pieces left over, seven baskets full.
points.apply: Say grace before every meal this Advent.

concl: Christ feeds us so that we may feed others.
The feast has begun at the altar.
2026-12-02.resolve: Prepare an Advent food basket for a poor family.

intro: Theme: “Built on rock.”
Not words but obedience; God the everlasting Rock; St Francis Xavier, a missionary built on Christ.

sub: The Father's will must be done.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Do one teaching of Jesus you have ignored.

sub: The same storms hit both houses.
q: Those of steadfast mind you keep in peace—in peace because they trust in you. Trust in the LORD forever, for in the LORD GOD you have an everlasting rock.

Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock. The rain fell, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house, but it did not fall, because it had been founded on rock.
points.apply: Build a daily habit of reading the Gospel.

sub: He left Europe for India in 1542.
He preached on the coasts of South India.
He died in sight of China.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation.

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Support a missionary or mission diocese this Advent.

concl: Faith that acts is a house on rock.
Like Xavier, let Christ be our foundation.
2026-12-03.resolve: Give an Advent offering to the missions.

intro: Theme: “Do you believe?”
God promises sight; Jesus asks for faith; faith sees in the dark.

sub: The deaf hear, the blind see.
q: On that day the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.
Then he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
points.apply: Pray for someone who cannot see God's hand in their life.

sub: The blind men followed and cried out.
q: Those of steadfast mind you keep in peace—in peace because they trust in you.

When he entered the house, the blind men came to him; and Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.” Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you.”
points.apply: Say “Yes, Lord, I believe” about your deepest need.

sub: The invisible God became visible in Christ.
We look on his face in prayer.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament today.

concl: Faith opens the eyes.
Christ is our light this Advent.
2026-12-04.resolve: Make a holy hour this First Friday or next week.

intro: Theme: “This is the way; walk in it.”
God waits to be gracious; Jesus has compassion; the Twelve are sent.

sub: He hears the cry of his people.
q: Therefore the LORD waits to be gracious to you; therefore he will rise up to show mercy to you. For the LORD is a God of justice; blessed are all those who wait for him.
When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
points.apply: Bring your deepest cry to God today.

sub: Advent is about finding the way.
q: And when you turn to the right or when you turn to the left, your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”
The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’
points.apply: Ask God for guidance in one decision.

q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Offer a free service to someone this week.

concl: God's compassion sends us out.
Walk in his way, and share what you have received.
2026-12-05.resolve: Pray each day of Advent for vocations from your parish.

intro: Theme: “Here is your God.”
God makes the desert bloom, friends carry the paralysed man, Christ forgives.

q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Say to those who are of a fearful heart, “Be strong, do not fear! Here is your God. He will come with vengeance, with terrible recompense. He will come and save you.”
Amazement seized all of them, and they glorified God and were filled with awe, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
points.apply: Encourage someone who is afraid.

sub: The friends would not give up.
q: Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
When he saw their faith, he said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven you.”
points.apply: Pray daily for a friend in need.

sub: Christ gives this authority to his Church.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits—who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the Pit, who crowns you with steadfast love and mercy.
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins—he said to the one who was paralyzed—“I say to you, stand up and take your bed and go to your home.”
points.apply: Go to Confession this Advent.

concl: God's coming makes everything bloom.
Let him forgive and raise you up.
2026-12-07.resolve: Bring someone with you to the parish Advent Confession service.

intro: Theme: “Full of grace.”
God promised the woman in Eden, preserved Mary from sin, and freed her to say yes.

The serpent's head will be crushed.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
A great portent appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
points.apply: Answer God's “Where are you?” in Confession.

sub: She is redeemed by Christ in a more exalted way.
God prepared a worthy home for his Son.
q: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.
And he came to her and said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today.

sub: Eve's knot is untied by Mary's yes.
q: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness.
For nothing will be impossible with God. Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
points.apply: Say yes to one thing God asks of you.

concl: God prepared Mary; he wants to prepare us.
With Mary, let us say yes.
2026-12-08.resolve: Pray the Rosary as a family this week.

intro: Theme: “Come to me.”
God never grows weary; Jesus gives rest; waiting on the Lord renews strength.

sub: He gives power to the faint.
q: Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable. He gives power to the faint, and strengthens the powerless.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Tell God honestly where you are tired.

sub: His burden is light because he carries it with us.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits—who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
points.apply: Help carry someone else's load this week.

sub: Waiting on God is active trust.
God chose the humble Juan Diego.
He reveals himself to the little ones.
q: But those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.

At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants.”
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in silent prayer today.

concl: The weary find rest in Christ.
Wait on the Lord, and rise.
2026-12-09.resolve: Visit the Blessed Sacrament once this week.

intro: Theme: “Do not fear, I will help you.”
God holds our hand, opens rivers in the desert, and makes the least great in his Kingdom.

points.apply: Pray “Lord, hold me” when afraid today.

sub: God opens rivers on bare heights.

Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink. As the scripture has said, “Out of the believer's heart shall flow rivers of living water.”
points.apply: Bring a dry area of your life to Jesus.

sub: John is the greatest of the prophets.
Baptism makes us children of the Kingdom.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Truly I tell you, among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
points.apply: Thank God for your Baptism.

concl: God holds us by the hand.
Little ones are great in his Kingdom.
2026-12-10.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises before Christmas.

God teaches for our good; excuses refuse every messenger; wisdom shows in deeds.

sub: God speaks like a longing father.
Obedience brings peace like a river.

The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’
points.apply: Read one commandment with the Catechism today.

But to what will I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling to one another, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn.’
points.apply: Drop one excuse you use with God.

sub: Jesus is a friend of sinners.
Our lives should show it too.
q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.
points.apply: Befriend someone others avoid.

concl: Stop excusing; start responding.
Let God's wisdom show in your deeds.
2026-12-11.resolve: Make an Advent examination on the Ten Commandments.

Elijah's fire, John's unrecognised coming, and Mary who carries Christ to a people.

He would return to prepare the way.

With the spirit and power of Elijah he will go before him, to turn the hearts of parents to their children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit to set your words on fire for good.

sub: The Son of Man too will suffer.
q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes. He will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents, so that I will not come and strike the land with a curse.

points.apply: Reconcile with a family member before Christmas.

q: When they met her, they all blessed her with one accord and said to her, “You are the glory of Jerusalem, you are the great boast of Israel, you are the great pride of our nation!”
A great portent appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
points.apply: Pray the Rosary for unborn children.

concl: God sends messengers to turn our hearts.
Mary brings Christ to us this Advent.
2026-12-12.resolve: Pray for the protection of unborn children this Advent.

God's promise shines from afar; Christ's authority is from heaven; truth asks for honesty.

sub: Balaam came to curse and blessed.
He saw the star from afar.
q: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near—a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel; it shall crush the borderlands of Moab, and the territory of all the Shethites.
Asking, “Where is the child who has been born king of the Jews? For we observed his star at its rising, and have come to pay him homage.”
points.apply: Put up your Christmas star with a prayer.

sub: His authority is from the Father.
He teaches as no one else.
q: Make me to know your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths. Lead me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation; for you I wait all day long.
When he entered the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority?”
points.apply: Let Christ's word have authority in one decision.

q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Did the baptism of John come from heaven, or was it of human origin? And they argued with one another, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’”
points.apply: Face one truth you have avoided.

concl: The star is rising; answer honestly.
In the evening of life we will be judged on love.
2026-12-14.resolve: Make a quiet holy hour this week.

God's humble remnant, the son who changed his mind, sinners who believed.

points.apply: Let someone else have the credit today.

Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Turn one “no” to God into a “yes” today.

sub: Tax collectors and prostitutes believed John.
The leaders saw and did not repent.
It is never too late to turn.
q: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.

points.apply: Go to Confession before Christmas.

concl: God builds with the humble.
Let your yes become action.
2026-12-15.resolve: Finish one good work you started and abandoned.

Heaven rains down the Saviour; John asks from prison; Jesus answers with signs.

And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Sing or pray the Rorate caeli this week.

q: Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptist has sent us to you to ask, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?’”
points.apply: Bring an honest doubt to Jesus.

sub: The blind see, the lame walk.
Blessed is the one not offended.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.

points.apply: Do one work of mercy as a sign of Christ.

concl: Christ answers our questions with his works.
Let us become his signs.
2026-12-16.resolve: Visit the poor or sick before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “O Wisdom, come!”
The O Antiphons begin; God keeps his promise to Judah; Jesus enters a real family tree.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
points.apply: Thank God for a promise he kept in your life.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to the Messiah, fourteen generations.
points.apply: Pray for your ancestors by name.

concl: God writes salvation through real families.
O Wisdom, come and teach us!
2026-12-17.resolve: Pray one O Antiphon each day until 23 December.

intro: Theme: “God with us.”

q: The days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal wisely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land. In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live in safety. And this is the name by which he will be called: “The LORD is our righteousness.”

Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
points.apply: Pray for just leaders in our country.

q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.

points.apply: Pray “Emmanuel, be with us” at each meal today.

q: Noah did this; he did all that God commanded him.
When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife.
points.apply: Do at once one thing God asks of you.

concl: God is with us in Jesus.
Like Joseph, let us listen and obey.
2026-12-18.resolve: Pray to St Joseph daily until Christmas.

points.apply: Pray for the protection of unborn life.

q: For you, O Lord, are my hope, my trust, O LORD, from my youth. Upon you I have leaned from my birth; it was you who took me from my mother's womb. My praise is continually of you.
This is what the Lord has done for me when he looked favorably on me and took away the disgrace I have endured among my people.
points.apply: Keep fifteen minutes of silence today.

2026-12-19.resolve: Make a silent half-hour before the crib on Christmas Eve.

points.apply: Renew your trust in one promise of God.

Christ comes, and the little ones leap for joy.

q: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, he also exalts. He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes and inherit a seat of honor.

He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts. He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty.
points.apply: Help a poor family prepare for Christmas.

sub: God promised Abraham a blessing for all.
q: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who curses you I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
He has helped his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy, according to the promise he made to our ancestors, to Abraham and to his descendants forever.
points.apply: Thank God for a promise kept in your family.

concl: God's power is shown in mercy to the humble.
Let our souls magnify the Lord.
2026-12-22.resolve: Pray the Magnificat every evening until Christmas.

intro: Theme: “His name is John.”
The messenger is born; the Lord comes as refiner's fire; silence breaks into praise.

sub: Jesus says John is that messenger.
He prepares the way of the Lord.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple. The messenger of the covenant in whom you delight—indeed, he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.
This is the one about whom it is written, ‘See, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.’
points.apply: Prepare one practical thing for Christmas with prayer.

sub: Christ baptises with Spirit and fire.
q: But who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap; he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the descendants of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, until they present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.
I baptize you with water for repentance, but one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
points.apply: Make your Christmas Confession today or tomorrow.

q: Listen to me, O coastlands, pay attention, you peoples from far away! The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And all of them were amazed. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.
points.apply: Praise God aloud for one mercy today.

concl: God names, calls and frees.
O Emmanuel, come!
2026-12-23.resolve: Be reconciled with someone before Christmas Eve.

intro: Theme: “The dawn from on high.”
Zechariah's Benedictus: God keeps his promise, John prepares the way, and the dawn breaks tonight.

sub: God visits and redeems his people.
q: When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, who shall come forth from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them. He has raised up a mighty savior for us in the house of his servant David.
points.apply: Pray the Benedictus this morning.

sub: Forgiveness of sins prepares the heart.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the forgiveness of their sins.
points.apply: Forgive someone before Christmas night.

sub: People in darkness see a great light.
He guides our feet into peace.
q: But for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings. You shall go out leaping like calves from the stall.
By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
points.apply: Make one act of peace in your family today.

concl: Advent ends in praise.
The dawn is breaking: Christ is near.
2026-12-24.resolve: Attend Christmas Mass with your whole family.

intro: Theme: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
Stephen, deacon and first martyr, dies like his Master, forgiving.

sub: A deacon who served the poor.
He preached with the Spirit's wisdom.
q: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you are to speak.

When they hand you over, do not worry about how you are to speak or what you are to say; for what you are to say will be given to you at that time; for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
points.apply: Serve the poor during the Christmas octave.

sub: The martyr's eyes are fixed on Christ.
q: Into your hand I commit my spirit; you have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.

But filled with the Holy Spirit, he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. “Look,” he said, “I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”
points.apply: Pray “Into your hands I commend my spirit” tonight.

sub: Stephen prays like Jesus while Saul watches.
q: Therefore I will allot him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he poured out himself to death, and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.

While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he died.
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who hurt you.

concl: The crib leads to the Cross, and the Cross to glory.
Forgive as Stephen forgave.
2026-12-26.resolve: Reconcile with someone during the Christmas octave.

intro: Theme: “Rachel weeping for her children.”
Joseph obeys, the Innocents die for Christ, and God gathers the little ones to himself.

sub: The angel speaks in a dream.
The Son relives Israel's journey to Egypt.
q: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.

Now after they had left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you; for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.”
points.apply: Obey promptly when God's will is clear.

sub: The children of Bethlehem are killed.
God hears the cry of mothers.
q: Thus says the LORD: A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.

When Herod saw that he had been tricked by the wise men, he was infuriated, and he sent and killed all the children in and around Bethlehem who were two years old or under, according to the time that he had learned from the wise men.
points.apply: Comfort a family that has lost a child.

points.h: The little ones belong to Christ
sub: The Innocents confessed Christ by dying.
God rescues his own from the snare.
q: We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
but Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them; for it is to such as these that the kingdom of heaven belongs.”
points.apply: Pray and work for unborn and endangered children.

concl: Herod's darkness does not have the last word.
Holy Innocents, pray for all children.
2026-12-28.resolve: Support a work that protects children this week.

intro: Theme: “My eyes have seen your salvation.”
Simeon, led by the Spirit, welcomes the light of the nations and foretells the sword.

points.h: The Lord comes to his temple
sub: The Child is carried into the Temple.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple. The messenger of the covenant in whom you delight—indeed, he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.

Guided by the Spirit, Simeon came into the temple; and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him what was customary under the law, Simeon took him in his arms and praised God, saying,
points.apply: Visit the Blessed Sacrament this week.

sub: The Servant is given as a light.
q: he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to restore the survivors of Israel; I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”

Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
points.apply: Pray for those who do not yet know Christ.

points.h: God carries us to the end
sub: God carries his people through sorrow.
q: even to your old age I am he, even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.

Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.”
points.apply: Visit an elderly person this week.

concl: The waiting of Israel is fulfilled in Simeon's arms.
Let us walk in the light.
2026-12-29.resolve: Pray the Nunc Dimittis each night this week.

intro: Theme: “She spoke about the child.”
Anna's faithful prayer, her joyful witness, and the quiet growth of Jesus at Nazareth.

sub: Fasting and prayer night and day.
q: even to your old age I am he, even when you turn gray I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry and will save.

There was also a prophet, Anna the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was of a great age, having lived with her husband seven years after her marriage, then as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.
points.apply: Pray for the elderly in your parish.

sub: The Spirit is poured on all.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
points.apply: Speak to one person about Jesus this week.

q: Train children in the right way, and when old, they will not stray.

When they had finished everything required by the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth. The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him.
points.apply: Teach a child a prayer this week.

concl: A life of prayer leads to joyful witness.
The world passes; God's will remains.
2026-12-30.resolve: Thank an elderly person who taught you the faith.

intro: Theme: “Grace upon grace.”
At the end of the year: the eternal Word, the light that darkness cannot overcome, and thanksgiving for every grace.

sub: God created all things by his word.
The Word was with God and was God.
Christ is Lord of every year.
q: In the beginning when God created the heavens and the earth, the earth was a formless void and darkness covered the face of the deep, while a wind from God swept over the face of the waters. Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being.
points.apply: Offer the coming year to Christ.

sub: The glory of the Lord has risen.
Christ is the light of the world.
Whoever follows him does not walk in darkness.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
Again Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
points.apply: Bring one darkness of this year to Confession.

sub: Teach us to count our days.
Begin the new year with thanksgiving.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. The law indeed was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Take part in the Te Deum tonight.

concl: Time belongs to Christ.
We end the year with thanks and begin it with Mary.
2026-12-31.resolve: Begin the new year at Mass on the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God.
